column1: # Hand readings for docs/diag-messages.tsv: id, grade, the condition the call runs under, and the note.
# Each line was read against the disassembly of the routine. Addresses are offsets in the object.

column3: a1 != 0 at the beqz a1 at 0xb8 (the level is still above the threshold)
column4: Hi-water timeout routine, level still above the threshold at +2332. Tag 2102 (li a0 at 0xdc), level 4, format "%s%d:  Timeout waiting for fifo to drain (level == 0x%x)." with "IR", the instance word at +2184 and the FIFO level read through gfx_pio_read_32 at 0x800208 plus the board base. Both paths after it reach kona_die with reason 6 (li a1,6 at 0x108).

column3: a1 == 0 at the beqz a1 at 0xb8 (the level has fallen); the delay slot at 0xbc has already loaded the banner into a1
column4:
Fallen branch of the hi-water timeout routine. Level 4, no arguments. The banner is "
kona_lowater_intr in kona_hiwater_timeout routine

", which names a different routine from the one that prints it. Then calls kona_lowater_intr with the board pointer (0x134) and returns; no kona_die on this path.

column3: kona_timeout (call at 0x3cc) returned 0: beqz v0 at 0x3d4 jumps to 0x490
column4: Hi-water arm failed: kona_timeout gave no timer handle, so the handle at +2336 is not stored. Level 4, format "%s%d:  Could not set hi water timeout!?!" with "IR" and the instance word. Falls straight into the 0x4b0 notice.

column3: same path as 0x4a0; no branch between the two calls
column4: Level 6 notice "Cannot automatically recover if pipe hangs." with no arguments. The routine then calls kona_die(board, 9) (li a1,9 in the delay slot at 0x4c0).

column3: word at +104 is nonzero (beqz v0 at 0x4ec not taken) and the timeout handle at +2336 is zero (beqz a1 at 0x4f8 taken to 0x584)
column4: Low-water routine finds the pipe backed up with no timer armed. Level 4, format "%s%d:  pipe was backed up without timeout being set." with "IR" and the instance word. The code after the call was not read.

column3: unconditional: no branch precedes the call on entry to kona_xg_intr_handler
column4: XG error interrupt handler entry. Bumps the per-board count in the statistics record (gfxinfo, indexed by the CPU number read from the fixed per-CPU word at -15328) and the word at +5268, then logs level 4 "%s%d: XG error interrupt received." with "IR" and the instance word. The routine's later calls were not read.

column3: bit 0x40 of s1 is set: andi v0,s1,0x40 at 0x138, beqz v0 at 0x13c skips to 0x168 when it is clear
column4: ODMA overflow. cmn_err_tag with tag 2120 (li a0 at 0x150), level 4, format "%s%d: odma overflow." with "IR" and the instance word. No kona_die; the handler goes on to the next interrupt bit.

column3: bit 0x1 of s1 is set: andi a1,s1,0x1 at 0xec, bnez a1 at 0xf0 jumps to 0x1f0
column4: Hi-water interrupt on the HIP2 path that should not occur. Level 4, format "%s%d: unexpected HIP2 graphics fifo hi-water interrupt.  Ignored.". The routine goes on with the next bit (b to 0xf8); no kona_die.

column3: bit 0x4 of s1 is set: andi t9,s1,0x4 at 0x108, bnez t9 at 0x10c jumps to 0x210
column4: Graphics FIFO overflow with data lost. Level 4, format "%s%d: graphics fifo overflow.  Data lost.  Resetting pipe.", then kona_die(board, 10) (li a1,10 at 0x230).

column3: bit 0x100 of s1 is set: andi a3,s1,0x100 at 0x164, bnez a3 at 0x168 jumps to 0x23c
column4: Parity error with data lost. Level 4, format "%s%d: parity error.  Data lost.  Resetting pipe.", then kona_die(board, 22) (li a1,22 at 0x25c).

column3: bit 0x400 of s1 is set: andi a5,s1,0x400 at 0x180, bnez a5 at 0x184 jumps to 0x268
column4: PIO overflow with data lost. Level 4, format "%s%d: PIO overflow.  Data lost.  Resetting pipe.", then kona_die(board, 13) (li a1,13 at 0x288).

column3: bit 0x800 of s1 is set: andi a6,s1,0x800 at 0x188, bnez a6 at 0x18c jumps to 0x294
column4: IDMA overflow with data lost. Level 4, format "%s%d: IDMA overflow.  Data lost.  Resetting pipe.", then kona_die(board, 14) (li a1,14 at 0x2b0). The format pointer is loaded in the delay slot at 0x190, so it is set on this path.
